name: SBI PO
fullName: State Bank of India – Probationary Officers Recruitment
conductingBody: State Bank of India (Central Recruitment & Promotion Department)
eligibility: Graduate in any discipline (final-year students may apply provisionally); 21–30 years (relaxation for reserved categories)

notification.summary: SBI PO 2026 (Advt. CRPD/PO/2026-27/09) is in progress: prelims were held on 1–2 Aug 2026, the prelims result was declared on 28 Aug 2026 and the mains was held on 12 Sep 2026; Phase III (psychometric test, group exercise and interview) is next. Reports mention ≈1,500 vacancies. Dates are from news portals; SBI's careers page could not be opened from the research environment.

pattern.notes: 20 minutes per section with separate timers. No sectional cut-off in recent SBI PO prelims (overall, category-wise cut-off; about 10× vacancies shortlisted). Prelims is qualifying only. Phase II mains (objective + descriptive) and Phase III (psychometric test, group exercise, interview) follow.

trendAnalysis.summary: SBI PO prelims has been easy-to-moderate in English and moderate in Quant and Reasoning; good attempts were ≈66–74 in Aug 2026. English (40 Qs) relies on RC (≈7–10), cloze (5–6), rearrangement/para-jumble (5), double fillers, word swap and error spotting, with new formats such as column-based sentence matching. Quant is DI-heavy (2–3 sets incl. caselets and missing-data tables) with quadratic/quantity-comparison, number series and arithmetic word problems. Reasoning is dominated by puzzles and seating arrangements (≈15–18 Qs: parallel-row, floor-flat, month/year puzzles) plus syllogism, inequality and quick misc questions (meaningful words, pairs).

resources.notes: SBI does not publish full PO question papers or answer keys. Official material: the detailed advertisement with exam pattern, and pre-examination training (PET) material for eligible reserved-category candidates on sbi.bank.in/web/careers; candidates can view their own marks after the final result. Previous papers available online are memory-based compilations by coaching institutes.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.

The rapid growth of platform-based work has blurred the line between employees and independent contractors. Delivery riders and ride-hailing drivers enjoy flexible hours, but they usually lack the health cover, paid leave and pension contributions that salaried workers take for granted. Platforms argue that classifying these workers as employees would raise costs and reduce the flexibility that many of them value. Labour advocates counter that flexibility is meaningless if a single accident can push a worker's family into debt. A middle path is now emerging in several countries: platforms contribute a small percentage of each transaction to a social-security fund, while workers retain the freedom to log in and out as they wish. Whether such schemes succeed will depend on how accurately earnings are recorded and how easily workers can claim benefits, since a fund that is hard to access offers little real protection.

Which of the following best captures the main idea of the passage?
options: Platform work should be banned because it is unsafe
The debate over social security for platform workers and a possible middle path
How platforms calculate their delivery charges
Labour advocates' opposition to flexible hours
questions.explanation: The passage presents both sides of the classification debate and then describes the emerging contribution-based middle path.

questions.question:

questions.question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
A. Instead, it was the steady rise in the number of small investors.
B. The stock market rally surprised many analysts this year.
C. Most had expected foreign investors to drive the gains.
D. Monthly SIP inflows, in particular, reached record levels.
E. Foreign funds, however, were net sellers for much of the period.
questions.explanation: B (rally surprised analysts) → C (they expected foreign investors) → E (however, foreigners sold) → A (instead, small investors) → D (SIP inflows in particular): BCEAD.

questions.question:
Rearrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph and choose the FIRST sentence.
A. This means a borrower's EMI changes soon after a policy rate change.
B. Many home loans in India are now linked to an external benchmark.
C. Borrowers should therefore track policy announcements closely.
D. The most common benchmark is the central bank's repo rate.
E. Earlier, banks could delay passing on rate cuts to customers.
questions.explanation: B introduces external-benchmark loans; D names the benchmark; A gives the effect; E contrasts with the past; C concludes. The first sentence is B.

A college has 1,600 students: 45% study Commerce, 35% Science and the rest Arts. 60% of Commerce students, 40% of Science students and 25% of Arts students are girls.

What is the total number of boys in the college?
questions.explanation: Commerce 720 (boys 40% = 288), Science 560 (boys 60% = 336), Arts 320 (boys 75% = 240). Total = 864.

questions.question:
A college has 1,600 students: 45% study Commerce, 35% Science and the rest Arts. 60% of Commerce students, 40% of Science students and 25% of Arts students are girls.

The number of girls in Science is what percent of the number of boys in Arts?
questions.explanation: Girls in Science = 40% of 560 = 224; boys in Arts = 75% of 320 = 240. 224/240 × 100 = 93⅓%.

questions.question:
A college has 1,600 students: 45% study Commerce, 35% Science and the rest Arts. 60% of Commerce students, 40% of Science students and 25% of Arts students are girls.

If 25% of the boys in Commerce move to Arts, what will be the ratio of girls to boys in Arts?
questions.explanation: Commerce boys = 288; 25% = 72 move. Arts boys = 240 + 72 = 312, girls = 80. Ratio 80 : 312 = 10 : 39.

questions.question:
Solve and compare.
I. x² + 3x − 40 = 0
II. y² − 13y + 40 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation: I: (x + 8)(x − 5) = 0 → x = −8, 5. II: (y − 5)(y − 8) = 0 → y = 5, 8. Every x is less than or equal to every y (5 = 5), so x ≤ y.

Eight persons sit in two parallel rows of four each. In Row 1, P, Q, R and S sit facing south; in Row 2, A, B, C and D sit facing north, so that each person faces exactly one person of the other row. P faces A. R sits at an extreme end of his row. Only one person sits between R and S. B sits second to the right of A. The person who faces S sits immediately to the left of B. Neither C nor P sits at an extreme end of the row.

Who faces Q?
questions.explanation: Columns from west to east — Row 1 (facing south): R, P, S, Q; Row 2 (facing north): D, A, C, B. Q faces B.

questions.question:
Eight persons sit in two parallel rows of four each. In Row 1, P, Q, R and S sit facing south; in Row 2, A, B, C and D sit facing north, so that each person faces exactly one person of the other row. P faces A. R sits at an extreme end of his row. Only one person sits between R and S. B sits second to the right of A. The person who faces S sits immediately to the left of B. Neither C nor P sits at an extreme end of the row.

Who sits immediately to the right of P?
questions.explanation: Row 1 faces south, so a person's right is towards the west. Row 1 west→east: R, P, S, Q. R is immediately to the right of P.

questions.question:

Neither C nor P sits at an extreme end of the row.

Which two persons sit at the extreme ends of Row 2?
questions.explanation: Working through the clues: Row 1 (west→east) R, P, S, Q and Row 2 (west→east) D, A, C, B. D and B sit at the ends of Row 2.

questions.question:
Seven persons L, M, N, O, P, Q and R have birthdays in seven different months of the same year — January, March, April, June, August, October and December (in calendar order; 'immediately before' refers to these seven months only). L's birthday is in a month that has 30 days. Only two persons have birthdays between L and Q. M's birthday is immediately before Q's. O's birthday is after Q's. R's birthday is immediately before M's. N's birthday is before P's. Neither N nor P has a birthday in a month that has 30 days.

Whose birthday is in June?
questions.explanation: Order: N (Jan), P (Mar), L (Apr), R (Jun), M (Aug), Q (Oct), O (Dec). R's birthday is in June.

questions.question:
Seven persons L, M, N, O, P, Q and R have birthdays in seven different months of the same year — January, March, April, June, August, October and December (in calendar order; 'immediately before' refers to these seven months only). L's birthday is in a month that has 30 days. Only two persons have birthdays between L and Q. M's birthday is immediately before Q's. O's birthday is after Q's. R's birthday is immediately before M's. N's birthday is before P's. Neither N nor P has a birthday in a month that has 30 days.

How many persons have birthdays between N and M?
questions.explanation: Order: N (Jan), P (Mar), L (Apr), R (Jun), M (Aug), Q (Oct), O (Dec). Between N and M: P, L and R — three.

questions.question:
Seven persons L, M, N, O, P, Q and R have birthdays in seven different months of the same year — January, March, April, June, August, October and December (in calendar order; 'immediately before' refers to these seven months only). L's birthday is in a month that has 30 days. Only two persons have birthdays between L and Q. M's birthday is immediately before Q's. O's birthday is after Q's. R's birthday is immediately before M's. N's birthday is before P's. Neither N nor P has a birthday in a month that has 30 days.

In which month is Q's birthday?
questions.explanation: L must be Apr or Jun; with two persons between L and Q, and R, M, Q consecutive with O after Q, only L = Apr, R = Jun, M = Aug, Q = Oct, O = Dec works. N and P take Jan and Mar. Q's birthday is in October.

questions.question:
Eight persons J, T, U, V, W, X, Y and Z live in a four-storey building (floor 1 is the bottom, floor 4 the top). Each floor has two flats — West and East — with one person in each flat. T lives in an East flat on an even-numbered floor. Z lives in the flat immediately below T's flat (same side, one floor lower). V lives on the same floor as Z. Y lives in a West flat on a floor below J's floor. Only one floor lies between U's floor and X's floor, and U lives in an East flat. W lives on floor 1.

Who lives in the West flat of floor 3?
questions.explanation: Floor 4: X (W), T (E); floor 3: V (W), Z (E); floor 2: J (W), U (E); floor 1: Y (W), W (E). V lives in 3-West.

questions.question:
Eight persons J, T, U, V, W, X, Y and Z live in a four-storey building (floor 1 is the bottom, floor 4 the top). Each floor has two flats — West and East — with one person in each flat. T lives in an East flat on an even-numbered floor. Z lives in the flat immediately below T's flat (same side, one floor lower). V lives on the same floor as Z. Y lives in a West flat on a floor below J's floor. Only one floor lies between U's floor and X's floor, and U lives in an East flat. W lives on floor 1.

Who lives on the same floor as U?
questions.explanation: Floor 2 has J (West) and U (East).

questions.question:
Eight persons J, T, U, V, W, X, Y and Z live in a four-storey building (floor 1 is the bottom, floor 4 the top). Each floor has two flats — West and East — with one person in each flat. T lives in an East flat on an even-numbered floor. Z lives in the flat immediately below T's flat (same side, one floor lower). V lives on the same floor as Z. Y lives in a West flat on a floor below J's floor. Only one floor lies between U's floor and X's floor, and U lives in an East flat. W lives on floor 1.

Which of the following statements is true?
options: X lives in the East flat of floor 4
W lives in the West flat of floor 1
questions.explanation: T cannot be in 2-East (Z and V would then fill floor 1, leaving no room for W), so T is 4-East, Z 3-East and V 3-West. U (East) must be 2-East with X on floor 4 (West). W is on floor 1, so Y is 1-West and J 2-West. Y (1-West) lives immediately below J (2-West).

questions.question:
Statements: Some apples are mangoes. All mangoes are grapes. No grape is a lemon.
Conclusions: I. Some apples are not lemons. II. No mango is a lemon.
questions.explanation: Apples that are mangoes are grapes and therefore not lemons (I follows). All mangoes are grapes and no grape is a lemon, so no mango is a lemon (II follows).

questions.question:
Statements: All doctors are nurses. Only a few nurses are teachers. No teacher is a lawyer.
Conclusions: I. Some doctors being teachers is a possibility. II. All nurses can be lawyers.
questions.explanation: Doctors (all nurses) may lie among the nurses who are teachers — I is possible. Some nurses are teachers and no teacher is a lawyer, so those nurses cannot be lawyers — II is false.

questions.question:
Statements: J > K ≥ L; M ≤ L < N; O ≥ M
Conclusions: I. J > M  II. O > K
questions.explanation: J > K ≥ L ≥ M gives J > M. O and K are linked only through M (O ≥ M ≤ L ≤ K), so no relation — only I follows.

questions.question:
Statements: A > B = C ≥ D; E ≤ D < F; G ≥ F
Conclusions: I. C > E  II. C = E
questions.explanation: C ≥ D ≥ E gives C ≥ E. Neither 'C > E' nor 'C = E' is definite alone, but together they cover all cases — either I or II follows.

questions.question: P is the husband of Q. R is the son of P. S is the daughter of Q. T is the wife of R. U is the son of T and R. How is S related to U?
questions.explanation: R and S are children of the couple P–Q, so S is R's sister. U is R's son, so S is U's (paternal) aunt.

questions.question: A man walks 4 km south, turns left and walks 3 km, turns left again and walks 10 km, then turns right and walks 5 km. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.explanation: South 4 → left (east) 3 → left (north) 10 → right (east) 5. Net: 8 km east, 6 km north. Distance √(64 + 36) = 10 km, towards the North-East.

questions.question: In a certain code, every consonant is replaced by its position in the English alphabet and every vowel is kept unchanged. 'FOCUS' is written as '6O3U19'. How is 'BASIC' written?
questions.explanation: B = 2, A stays, S = 19, I stays, C = 3 → 2A19I3.

questions.question: Using the 1st, 3rd, 6th and 7th letters of the word 'DIGITAL', exactly how many meaningful English words can be formed? If exactly one, give its third letter; if none, answer X; if more than one, answer Z.
questions.explanation: The letters are D, G, A, L, which form only 'GLAD'. Its third letter is A.

questions.question: Ravi ranks 9th from the top and 26th from the bottom in his class. How many students are in the class?
